front: Who were the Big Three at Paris in 1919?
back: Woodrow Wilson (USA), Georges Clemenceau (France) and David Lloyd George (Britain).

front: When did the Paris Peace Conference open?

back: Wilson's programme for peace (8 January 1918): open diplomacy, freedom of the seas, free trade, disarmament, self-determination and a League of Nations.
The right of a nationality to decide how it is governed, usually by forming its own state.

front: Why did Clemenceau want a harsh peace?
back: France had been invaded in 1870 and 1914, lost about 1.3-1.4 million soldiers (estimate) and had its north-east devastated, so he wanted security and reparations.

front: Why did Lloyd George privately want a moderate peace?
back: To revive trade with Germany, avoid a war of revenge and stop Germany turning to communism (Fontainebleau Memorandum, March 1919).
The Rhineland stayed German but was demilitarised and occupied by Allied troops for fifteen years.

front: Why did the USA not join the League?
back: The US Senate rejected the Treaty of Versailles (November 1919 and March 1920).

front: Who wrote The Economic Consequences of the Peace (1919)?
back: John Maynard Keynes, who argued that reparations would damage Europe's economy.
